hard_case: the test body declares its own `cost`, so `cost(150)` never reaches the imported owner

truth.toolchain: node 22.22.0; jest 30.5.2, ts-jest 29.4.14, typescript 5.9.3; edit applied by hand and the test command run on the whole package

mutants.equivalence_review: not equivalent: the owner returns 130 for 150 instead of 140, but the test's `cost` is a body-local arrow that never calls it

reasoning: The default-exported owner changes `amount - 10` to `amount - 20`. The test imports it as `cost` but its body declares `const cost = (amount) => amount - 10`, so `expect(cost(150)).toBe(140)` calls the body-local arrow and passes on both versions. RIPR-SPEC-0251 example 3: a body declaration of `cost` earns no owner credit, not `exposed`. ripr finds no call of the owner and reports `no_static_path`, an abstention the spec allows (not `exposed`) for the not-discriminated truth.
